evals.prompt: Add a Callout component to Menlo's design system: a soft-tinted box with an optional icon and title, for tips inside forms. It should support the usual tones.
evals.expected_output: src/ui/Menlo.Ui/Components/MnlCallout.razor inheriting MnlComponent with Attributes splatted on the root and RootClass('mnl-callout'), Tone as MnlTone, Icon as MnlIconName?, Title string?, ChildContent; MnlCallout.razor.css using --mnl-*-soft and role tokens selected by data-tone; a gallery example with Code; a component test with Rendered.ComponentAsync; design-system.md updated.

assertions.text: The component is MnlCallout.razor in src/ui/Menlo.Ui/Components, inherits MnlComponent, and puts @attributes=Attributes and RootClass on its root
Tone uses the shared MnlTone enum and Icon uses MnlIconName, not strings
The scoped .razor.css uses --mnl-* role tokens (for example --mnl-info-soft) and data-tone selectors, with no hex colours or pixel spacing and no inline style
The component has no @inject and no reference to budgets, Menlo.Api or Menlo.Lib
An example with its markup is added to a Gallery section
A test in src/ui/Menlo.Ui.Tests renders it with Rendered.ComponentAsync and checks tone and optional parts

evals.prompt: On a page I need to show each category's status as 'Over budget' in red when spending passed the plan, and its type (Income/Expense) as a label. Which components and tones should I use? Just tell me, with a snippet.
evals.expected_output: MnlBadge with Tone=MnlTone.Error for 'Over budget' (a status), MnlTag for Income/Expense (a descriptive label). The decision of which tone comes from the view model, and they sit in an MnlCluster.

assertions.text: Recommends MnlBadge with MnlTone.Error for the over-budget status
Recommends MnlTag (not a badge) for Income/Expense
Says the tone or over-budget decision comes from the view model, not computed in the markup
Does not suggest a hex colour, an inline style or a new CSS class for the red

evals.prompt: The success green looks too bright in dark mode on our new 'savings' tile. Make the tile's background a softer green in both themes.
evals.expected_output: Uses the existing --mnl-success-soft role token (or adds a new role token in tokens.css built from --ctp-green with light-dark/color-mix), applied in the tile's scoped CSS; no hex values in component CSS; checks /design or the page in both themes.

assertions.text: Uses --mnl-success-soft or defines a new --mnl-* role in tokens.css rather than a literal colour in the component
The change works for both Latte and Mocha (via the role token, light-dark or color-mix), not a dark-only override
No hex colour is added outside tokens.css
Says to check the result in light and dark mode (for example on /design)
